name: Arman Financial Services Ltd
tagline: Ahmedabad NBFC (two-wheeler finance + group microfinance via Namra) coming out of the sector-wide MFI asset-quality cycle with a clean live turnaround - Q1 FY27 back to profit (Rs 45 Cr vs Rs 15 Cr loss), AUM +36%, GNPA down from a 3.8% peak to 2.6% - trading ~11-15x on a normalising earnings run-rate
business_overview: Arman Financial Services is an Ahmedabad-based NBFC promoted by Jayendra Patel, offering Two-Wheeler Finance, Group-Based Microfinance, and Micro-Enterprise (MSME) Loans, largely through subsidiary Namra Finance, across 392 MFI branches serving ~6.56 lakh active customers in 11 states.

fundamentals_narrative: FY26 was the cycle trough - PAT Rs 57 Cr (+9%), ROE 6.26%, full-year credit costs Rs 150 Cr - reflecting the broad Indian-microfinance FY24-25 asset-quality stress. Q1 FY27 is a clean inflection: consolidated AUM Rs 2,925 Cr (+35.7% YoY), record disbursements Rs 686 Cr (+76%), gross income Rs 202 Cr (+33.7%), and a swing back to Rs 45.2 Cr net profit from a Rs 14.6 Cr loss a year earlier; MFI subsidiary Namra Finance turned to Rs 30 Cr PAT from a Rs 28 Cr loss. GNPA has fallen from a 3.8% peak to 2.59%. Management guides credit costs settling toward ~3-3.5% and holds a Rs 5,000 Cr AUM aspiration (no firm date). Trailing P/E (~48x) is optically high on trough earnings; on the Q1 FY27 annualised run-rate the stock is ~11-15x. Leverage (D/E 1.43) is normal for a lending book but amplifies any renewed asset-quality slippage, and the sector remains politically/regulatorily sensitive (loan-waiver / state-intervention risk).

verdict_headline: Well-run, well-covered NBFC-MFI with a clean, now-evidenced turnaround out of the sector stress cycle and an undemanding forward multiple - but it is one quarter deep, the sector is politically sensitive, and a literal 10x from this base is a stretch
verdict_reasoning: Best-in-peer-group asset quality through the cycle and a genuine Q1 FY27 inflection - AUM +35.7% YoY, disbursements +76%, PAT Rs 45.2 Cr vs a Rs 14.6 Cr loss, Namra Finance back to Rs 30 Cr PAT, GNPA down from a 3.8% peak to 2.59%.
On trailing FY26 (trough) EPS the P/E is ~48x, but on the Q1 FY27 annualised run-rate it is ~11-15x - the multiple is undemanding if the turnaround holds.

annual_report_findings: FY26 the trough of the cycle: PAT Rs 57 Cr (+9%), ROAA 2.28%, ROE 6.26%; full-year provisions/write-offs Rs 150 Cr.
AUM Rs 2,728 Cr FY26 (+22%); MFI AUM Rs 1,999 Cr (+19%), standalone (2W + MSME) Rs 730 Cr (+30%); disbursements Rs 2,433 Cr (+42%).
Asset quality bottomed and began improving within FY26: GNPA 3.4%, NNPA 0.95% at year-end vs a 3.8% peak.
Funded via a mix of bank lines and a Dec-2023 QIP (Rs 230 Cr at Rs 2,195); promoter holding ~22%, institutions (WhiteOak, Sundaram, UTI, Kotak Life) on the register.
Best-in-peer-group asset quality through the cycle - Arman's peak GNPA far below Fusion/Spandana-type peers that ran double-digit GNPA.
Low equity float (~1.05 Cr shares) makes the stock volatile and the trailing multiple noisy.
quarterly_trend: Q1 FY26: net loss Rs 14.6 Cr (Namra loss Rs 28 Cr) - the bottom.
H2 FY26: profitability recovering quarter by quarter as credit costs eased; GNPA trending down.
Q4 FY26: profit rebound; FY26 PAT Rs 57 Cr.
Q1 FY27: PAT Rs 45.2 Cr, AUM +35.7% YoY, disbursements +76%, GNPA 2.59%, Namra PAT Rs 30 Cr - full turnaround with growth re-accelerating.
recent_announcements: Q1 FY27 record AUM and disbursements; return to profit.
Rs 5,000 Cr AUM aspiration reiterated (no firm timeline).
Deliberate split of lending vs collections teams to tighten underwriting (per bennathan / concall).
No fresh equity raise announced in the period reviewed; no pledge red flag surfaced.
key_new_facts: The turnaround is now evidenced, not hoped-for: Q1 FY27 profit, Namra profitable, GNPA 3.8% -> 2.59%, disbursements +76%.
On a normalised earnings run-rate the stock is ~11-15x forward, not the ~48x the trailing P/E shows.
Growth is re-accelerating (AUM +22% FY26 -> +35.7% Q1 FY27) even as asset quality improves - the healthy combination.
Standalone (2W + MSME) book growing faster (+30%) than MFI - a modest diversification away from pure microfinance.
open_questions: Does credit cost actually settle at 3-3.5% or is there a second leg of MFI stress (monsoon, state elections, MFIN guardrail changes)?
Timeline for the Rs 5,000 Cr AUM aspiration - management has given none.
Will Arman need to raise equity to fund AUM toward Rs 5,000 Cr at D/E ~1.4-1.5, and at what price?
Sustainable through-cycle ROE - historically ~20%+, but the last three years averaged high-single-digits.
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Medium. The turnaround is real and now evidenced (Q1 FY27 profit, GNPA down, Namra profitable, AUM +36%) and the forward multiple is undemanding, but it is one clean quarter out of a stress cycle in a politically sensitive sector, and a literal 10x from a Rs 2,071 Cr NBFC is a stretch - held at Medium with an unconfirmed caveat.

track_record.note: FY22-FY23 cleared both bars (revenue growth >=10% and ROCE >=15% at Arman's historical ~20%+ ROE). FY24, FY25, FY26 failed the ROCE>=15% bar (ROE fell to 6-11%) during the sector-wide MFI asset-quality cycle, though operating income kept growing >10%. Q1 FY27 points back toward clearing it.
